messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a big spike in retries and 503s for svc/gpu-infer in us-west2-e starting ~21:02 UTC. Error rate up ~8x, tail latency also rising. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/board/xyz?srv=gpu-infer

anil: thanks — any node or AZ concentration?

maria: mostly node-gpu-122 and node-gpu-124. CPU fine, NIC queues pegged, but interestingly only east-west traffic to those nodes is failing (client pod -> gpu pod). North-south (ingress) to same svc is OK.

kai: can you paste ipvs stats and endpoints dump? could be L4 hash imbalance / flow steering oddness with the new NIC drivers.

maria: paste below (trimmed):
```
$ ipvsadm -L -n --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
 -> 10.45.12.7:8500 rr persistent 0
   -> 10.42.3.11:8500             100         23456       0         0%
   -> 10.42.7.9:8500               5        987623   23432      98%
   -> 10.42.9.3:8500              10         3452    12      0%

Conn: 120000   InPKTS: 7.2M   OutPKTS: 7.1M
```

maria: note one endpoint has 98% of hits while others are barely used — and that endpoint is the node-gpu-122 pod.

julia: kubectl get endpoints svc/gpu-infer -o wide shows:
```
NAME         ENDPOINTS                       AGE
svc/gpu-infer   10.42.3.11:8500,10.42.7.9:8500,10.42.9.3:8500   3d
```
The pod backing 10.42.7.9 is node-gpu-122 and is the heavy one.

ethan: checking dmesg on node-gpu-122 — seeing repeated mlx5 driver messages + rcu stalls and some NETDEV WATCHDOG entries. Also a handful of "ip_vs: conn reuse from wrong dest" logs around the same time.

kai: that pattern smells like asymmetric hashing + NIC-level offload mismatch. If the NIC's RSS/steering isn't consistent for certain packet 5-tuples we can end up funneling most flows to a single RX queue and therefore single CPU/core handling the flows -> IPVS ends up steering them to one endpoint more due to conntrack artifacts.

anil: did we recently push a kernel or firmware update to that rack?

maria: yes — we rolled out a NIC firmware bump and kernel patch to the west2 GPU fleet at 19:40 for an unrelated RDMA perf fix. Rollout was 50% canary -> full in that rack. node-gpu-122 got the update.

julia: quick reproduction check: from a client pod in same node pool, we see SYNs hitting different src ports but responses always coming from the same server IP.

maria: tried `ss -tn sport = :<ephemeral>` and saw many connections in CLOSE-WAIT on the heavy endpoint. Rest of endpoints show transient connections.

anil: immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon node-gpu-122 and move new pods off it, 2) restart kube-proxy on that node to rebuild IPVS state, 3) rollback NIC firmware on affected hosts if diagnosis confirms.

kai: also can toggle service sessionAffinity to ClientIP temporarily to force consistent hashing by client. That will change distribution but might reduce retries while we debug.

maria: I rolled kube-proxy restart on node-gpu-122 — reverted IPVS state, but the distribution snapped back to the single heavy endpoint within minutes. So restart alone didn't help.

ethan: kernel logs show the firmware update enabled a new RSS hashing mode (toeplitz -> symmetric-hash), but for a portion of flows the NIC still reports old hash values. That mixed state could easily cause conntrack lookups to mismatch and fall back to the same local conn entry.

julia: can we force the NIC to use symmetric hash via ethtool and test?

maria: trying ethtool -N eth0 rx-flow-hash tcp4 sdfn 0x3 0x0 now — will report.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3420 (high retry rate gpu-infer us-west2-e). Paging on-call. https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-3420

maria: ethtool change temporarily rebalanced flows across endpoints; retry rate dropped ~70% for the last 5m. But it's not a long-term config we want to push without review.

anil: good diagnostic. Action plan proposal: 1) cordon & drain node-gpu-122 and node-gpu-124 to remove hot endpoints from rotation, 2) roll back the NIC firmware on the affected rack to previous known-good, 3) schedule controlled re-do of firmware with additional NIC hashing flags, 4) add an automated check in the firmware rollout job to validate symmetric RSS across all nodes before marking as successful.

kai: and add a kube-proxy config validation to the canary job — ensure IPVS conntrack behavior matches expected flows (we can run a small flow-generator test to validate distribution).

julia: I'll open a runbook PR that codifies the ethtool flag we used and the drain steps.

maria: starting cordon/drain now for node-gpu-122. Will post updates.

ethan: creating rollback MR for NIC firmware. Target immediate rollback to 2025-11-13 firmware on the rack.

maria: cordon complete, pods re-scheduled off node-gpu-122; metrics show tail retries dropping. Keeping node cordoned until rollback validated.

anil: good. For postmortem: track exact kernel/firmware versions + heap of ipvs logs and the ethtool commands we ran. Also consider adding probe in the fleet deploy pipeline that verifies no per-node asymmetric RSS reports.

maria: noted — will attach logs to INC-2026-3420 and schedule a postmortem once rollback finished. Thanks all :thumbsup:
